name: 2C-EF
summary: 2C-EF, also known as 4-(2-fluoroethyl)-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families. It is the 2C analogue of the DOx psychedelic DOEF. The drug is taken orally. 2C-EF was first described in the literature by Alexander Shulgin in his 1991 book PiHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved.

pharmacology.text: 2C-EF is a serotonergic psychedelic and hence presumably acts as a serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist.

uses.text: While 2C-EF was briefly mentioned by Alexander Shulgin in his book PiHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved), its properties and effects were not described.
